To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) miRNA expression profiles can accurately classify tumor samples away from normal tissue samples, and (2) miRNA expression patterns in plasma can be used to distinguish colorectal cancer patients from healthy volunteers.

We have identified several miRNAs that distinguish colorectal cancer tumors from normal adjacent tissue and that distinguish colorectal tumor patients from healthy volunteers based on plasma miRNA profiles.

the miRNA expression profiles of tumor samples from colorectral cancer patients differ from those of the matched NAT samples, that the miRNA profiles of plasma from colorectal patients are distinct from those of healthy volunteers, and that the miRNA signature of colorectal cancer in plasma is distinct from the signature of the tumor tissue itself.
In summary, our research is concerned with
miRNA profiling and miRNA based diagnostic marker discovery for colorectal cancer.
the discovery and characterization of miRNAs in colorectal cancer.

the identification of miRNAs that distinguish colorectal cancer tissue samples from normal tissue samples from the same patients and with the identification of circulating miRNAs that may serve as non invasive biomarkers of colorectal cancer.

the miRNome is differentially expressed in tumor tissue and plasma from colorectral cancer patients, and that there are miRNAs that can be identified as potential markers for colorectal cancer.

The main takeaway from our work is that

we are able to accurately classify tumor and NAT samples based on miRNA profiling alone and we identify a set of miRNAs whose expression levels in plasma are altered in colorectal cancer patients versus healthy volunteers.

miRNA profiling is a robust, high quality method for distinguishing between tumor and normal tissue samples and that the plasma miRNome is a rich source of biomarkers that can distinguish between colorectal cancer patients from healthy volunteers.
